instructions: Blackwall is an autonomous Agentic Security Firewall designed to intercept execution flows at machine speed before rogue AI agents can perform unauthorized OS/network actions. The primary entry point is the Blackwall MCP Gateway — a standalone local daemon (src/blackwall/gateway/ + src/blackwall/cli.py) that intercepts MCP tool calls on localhost:9229 and evaluates them via the SyncResolver pipeline. Verify architecture invariants across Blackwall Core (single-host daemon + MCP Gateway) and Blackwall Enterprise Mesh (multi-host security mesh under src/blackwall/enterprise/). The gateway MUST NOT contain agent-specific coupling (no Hermes, no Antigravity-specific, no Warp-specific logic). Ensure strict Pydantic v2 validation, 100% GCP Vertex AI Mode compliance (paid tier only, no free tier, no AI Studio keys), TDD/BDD test coverage, and resource budget compliance for the 2019 Intel MacBook Pro baseline.

rules.rule: 100% GCP Vertex AI Mode (Paid Tier Only) Vendor Compliance: There is no free tier for Vertex AI — it is exclusively paid via GCP billing credits (300+ RPM quota). Ensure google-genai clients instantiate with vertexai=True, require GCP_PROJECT / GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT via Application Default Credentials (ADC). Flag any PR reintroducing Google AI Studio API key configurations (GEMINI_API_KEY, LLM_API_KEY, BACKUP_LLM_API_KEY), free-tier rate limit fallbacks (e.g. 15 RPM caps), or standard-tier rate limit logic. Note: VirusTotal GTI free-tier rate limits (4 queries/60s) are a separate third-party constraint and must NOT be stripped.

Core Tier Architecture & Zero-eBPF Integrity: Verify Blackwall Core (src/blackwall/ outside enterprise/) remains a lightweight single-host daemon containing zero imports or dependencies on ZeroMQ, NATS, or eBPF C headers.

Enterprise Subsystem Modularization: Verify all enterprise capabilities (eBPF kernel probes, ZeroMQ threat mesh, Vault sidecars, sandboxes, forensic engine, advanced threat detection) are cleanly isolated under src/blackwall/enterprise/.

Enterprise Boundary Review Scope: For code under src/blackwall/enterprise/, review only for Core/Enterprise boundary violations and shared interface compatibility. Do not flag Enterprise-internal pillar implementations (eBPF drivers, ZeroMQ mesh, Vault sidecar, pipeline wrappers, forensics engine) as violations — these are intentional Enterprise-only features.

Advanced Threat Detection (Pillar 6) Isolation & Model Validation: Verify Pillar 6 components (including ActiveReactionEngine, InboundProtocolFilter, PromptInjectionScanner, AgentQuotaEnforcer) reside under src/blackwall/enterprise/advanced_threat_detection/ and Pydantic v2 data models enforce UUID v4 identifiers, UTC timezone awareness with zero offset (utcoffset == 0), score bounds [0.0, 1.0], non-negative usage limits, string enums, and mandatory evidence-derived evaluation containment.

Async Interception Pipeline Resolver Order: Verify SyncResolver execution flow strictly maintains: Rate Check -> ContextHygiene Sanitization -> Threat Signature Graph (TSG) Check -> Codebase Memory MCP AST Query -> Conditional GTI Validation -> Score Aggregation -> Threshold Verdict.
SQL Parameterization Hygiene: Flag any SQL query that interpolates variables directly into an f-string without parameterized bindings. All dynamic values must be passed as bound parameters.

Synthetic Honey-Token & Secret Masking Compliance: Environment variable readers in src/blackwall/enterprise/identity/ must replace sensitive credentials (AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, KUBECONFIG) with synthetic honey-tokens (BW_SYNTHETIC_*) and route JIT swaps via hashicorp-vault-mcp.

Forensic Engine Dual-Mode & AST Resolution Integrity: Verify ForensicTriageEngine supports primary Ollama open-weight LLM triage with automatic failover to LightweightForensicParser when GPU/Ollama is offline. Ensure LightweightForensicParser AST inspection resolves fully qualified callee names (e.g. os.system, subprocess.Popen) rather than bare attribute names.

Test-Driven Development (TDD) & BDD Coverage: Flag any PR modifying src/ without corresponding unit or integration tests under tests/, property-based tests under tests/property/, and BDD feature scenarios in tests/features/.
Secret Scanner Hygiene in Test Artifacts: Ensure test files contain no live cloud credential patterns or high-entropy secret prefixes (e.g. AWS_KEY_<digits>).
Process Group Cleanup & Audit Hook Scoping: Verify sys.addaudithook registrations in tests are deferred to function scope and background test processes clean up process groups via os.killpg.

Attacker Identification & Reporting Integrity: Verify Attacker Identification & Reporting components (AttackerIdentityExtractor, AttackerProfile, IncidentReportGenerator) enforce Pydantic v2 validation (SHA-256 fingerprint, UTC timestamps, [0.0, 1.0] risk scores), process sanitized context, and fail-closed cleanly.

MCP Gateway Architecture Invariants: Verify gateway components under src/blackwall/gateway/ enforce: (1) HTTP transport binds to 127.0.0.1 by default with Origin/Host header validation, (2) JSON-RPC request id tracking for concurrent call isolation, (3) BLOCK verdicts synthesize error code -32603 with bounded generic messages (no internal threat reasoning leaked), (4) ALLOW verdicts forward original payloads unchanged to downstream tool servers, (5) daemon mode writes PID to ~/.blackwall/blackwall.pid with graceful SIGTERM shutdown.

Gateway Agent Agnosticism: The MCP Gateway (src/blackwall/gateway/ and src/blackwall/cli.py) MUST NOT contain hardcoded references, special-case logic, or configuration for any specific agent runtime (Hermes Agent, Antigravity, Warp Terminal, Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.). All agent interaction must be purely via standard MCP protocol. Flag any PR introducing agent-specific coupling in the gateway layer.

Gateway Resource Budget (2019 Intel MacBook Pro Baseline): Blackwall Core gateway components must operate within: ≤60MB idle RAM, ≤150MB active RAM, ~0% idle CPU, <5% active CPU per call, <2s startup, ≤50MB disk. Flag PRs introducing polling loops, background threads, or eager module loading that would violate these budgets.

PR Description Grouping: Group changes by Blackwall component: (1) MCP Gateway (src/blackwall/gateway/, src/blackwall/cli.py), (2) Core Engine (SyncResolver, policy, threat graph, attribution), (3) Enterprise Mesh (src/blackwall/enterprise/). Highlight changes affecting security resolvers, protocol transports, eBPF probes, or MCP adapters.

Dual-Tiered GCP Evaluation Architecture & Zero-SaaS Invariants: Threat evaluation pipelines must use Tier 1 (ADK Adversarial Harness in 100% GCP Vertex AI mode) or Tier 2 (Cybench on Cloud Run with gVisor microVMs) with Google Cloud Vertex AI Gen AI Evaluation Service (EvalTask) and Google Cloud Trace. Third-party SaaS evaluation tokens (WANDB_API_KEY) and Weave dependencies are deprecated and prohibited.

Performance & Async Safety: Focus code suggestions strictly on performance bottlenecks, thread safety, async coroutine safety, and security vulnerabilities. Ensure suggestions conform to Python 3.11+ async patterns and avoid deprecated decorators like @unittest_run_loop.
